entries.definition: unshaken in purpose
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The flat negative of the same idea - the purpose simply did not move, without the note of fear faced down in *undaunted*.

entries.definition: make illegal payments to in exchange for favors or influence
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the payment as the offence it is, an accusation rather than the sardonic understatement of *buy*.

entries.definition: make illegal payments to in exchange for favors or influence
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain word for a purchase turned on a person, so the contempt lies in the implication - they had a price - where *bribe* states the illegality outright.
examples: They said the inspector had been bought and would report whatever he was told.

entries.definition: having the nature of vice
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the thing as vice itself rather than describing a fault in it, which makes it absolute where *wicked* is merely damning.

entries.definition: extremely wicked, deeply criminal
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and heavy-syllabled, delivering the same extreme-and-criminal verdict as *heinous* in a more elevated register.

entries.definition: (of an actor or role) being or playing the villain
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A casting word: it marks the villain's part, or the actor filling it, and condemns nobody.
examples: Iago is the heavy role in ‘Othello’

entries.definition: extremely wicked, deeply criminal
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The blunt public condemnation, wickedness pitched so far into the criminal that the word works almost as a sentence.

entries.definition: characterized by iniquity; wicked because it is believed to be a sin
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The gravest of its group, weighing the wrong as an enormity rather than simply logging it as sin like *sinful*.

entries.definition: insusceptible of reform
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Pictures reform as recovery and denies it — nothing here can be got back.

entries.definition: insusceptible of reform
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The heaviest of these four, since redemption is what it withholds: a final verdict rather than a prognosis.

entries.definition: extremely wicked
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Condemns the wickedness in the abstract, where *villainous* points instead at the one committing it.

entries.definition: liable to sin
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest here by a wide margin: it concedes only that sin is possible, not that any has been done.

entries.definition: characterized by iniquity; wicked because it is believed to be a sin
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plainest naming of wickedness-as-sin, condemnatory without the swell of *iniquitous*.
examples: he said it was sinful to wear lipstick

entries.definition: characterized by iniquity; wicked because it is believed to be a sin
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Measures the wickedness as distance from godliness, so the fault is a standing away rather than *sinful*'s committed offence.

entries.definition: insusceptible of reform
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same refusal built on a blunt negative prefix, more workaday in sound than *irredeemable*.

entries.definition: insusceptible of reform
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flattest of the group, stating only that reform will not take, with none of *irredeemable*'s note of lost salvation.

entries.definition: having the nature of vice
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Presents vice as the settled bent of the thing, so it sounds like a diagnosis of character beside *evil*'s flat sentence.

entries.definition: extremely wicked
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Casts the extreme wickedness as a villain's, making it a fact of character rather than of the deed.

entries.definition: morally bad in principle or practice
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain, unhedged moral verdict, and it covers both the settled principle and the actual practice rather than choosing between them.

entries.definition: deprive somebody of something by deceit
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The hardest word here: the lie has a victim who is out something, and the loss is built into the charge.

entries.definition: deprive somebody of something by deceit
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal, and the pettiness is the sting — the same deceitful taking as *cheat*, cut down to something small and mean.

entries.definition: be false to; be dishonest with
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain, flat accusation of bad faith — it names the dishonesty and stops there, without saying what anyone got out of it.
examples: He deceived the friend who had trusted him most.

entries.definition: be false to; be dishonest with
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Heavier than *deceive* because the falseness is aimed at the other person's mind, leaving them settled in something untrue.

entries.definition: the trait of lacking enthusiasm for or interest in things generally
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The heaviest word here for the same trait: caring about nothing, weighed as a fault rather than merely reported.

entries.definition: the trait of lacking enthusiasm for or interest in things generally
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the want of enthusiasm or interest as a settled disposition, stating it without the reproach *apathy* attaches to the same trait.
examples: Years of illness had left him in a settled indifference to everything around him.

entries.definition: inactivity resulting from lethargy and lack of vigor or energy
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Traces the inactivity to lethargy and drained energy, so it reads as something suffered rather than a withholding.

entries.definition: the trait of lacking enthusiasm for or interest in things generally
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Casts the missing interest as feeling gone dull rather than a stance taken, which blunts the blame *apathy* carries.

entries.definition: the trait of remaining inactive; a lack of initiative
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flattest member: staying inactive and starting nothing, with no claim about what is or isn't felt underneath.
